components.name: CabButton
components.description: An arcade-style button with a glossy face that presses into its coloured base. Renders a native `<button>`; use it for actions, not navigation.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual weight. `primary` is the one main action on a view; `secondary` supports it; `ghost` is low emphasis.

props.name: size
props.description: Control size.

props.name: type
props.description: Native button type. Defaults to `button` so it never submits a form by accident.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the button using the native `disabled` attribute.

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows a spinner, sets `aria-busy`, and ignores clicks while staying focusable.

a11y.summary: An arcade-style button for actions. The glossy face presses down into its coloured base when activated. Use `primary` for the single main action on a view, `secondary` for supporting actions, and `ghost` for low-emphasis ones. Use a link, not a button, for navigation.
a11y.pattern: [WAI-ARIA APG: Button](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/button/). Rendered as a native `<button>`, so role, focus and activation come from the browser.
a11y.keyboard:
| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves focus to and from the button. |
| Enter | Activates the button. |
| Space | Activates the button. |
a11y.focus: A 3px purple ring (`--cab-color-focus-ring`) with a 3px offset appears on keyboard focus only (`:focus-visible`). A `loading` button stays focusable so focus is never lost mid-action; a `disabled` button is removed from the tab order by the browser.
a11y.screenReader: Announced as "*label*, button". While `loading`, `aria-busy="true"` is set and the spinner is hidden from assistive tech, so the label stays the accessible name. Disabled buttons are announced as dimmed/unavailable. Icon-only buttons are not supported: always give the button visible text.

examples.name: Basic
examples.code:
<!-- A primary action button. -->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { CabButton } from '@eltonbautista/vue'
</script>

<template>
  <CabButton @click="() => {}">Book a seat</CabButton>
</template>

examples.description: All three variants, plus loading and disabled states.

components.name: CabCard
components.description: A content container with a soft ledge, for grouping a title, media, text and actions. Not interactive by itself; pass `href` to make the whole card a link through its title.

props.name: as
props.description: Element to render. `article` for self-contained content (default), `section` or `div` otherwise.

props.name: title
props.description: Card title, rendered as a heading.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Heading level for the title, to fit the page outline.

props.name: href
props.description: Makes the title a link and stretches its hit area over the whole card.

slots.name: media
slots.description: Image or illustration above the content. Give images meaningful `alt` text, or `alt=""` if decorative.

slots.name: footer
slots.description: Actions or meta row at the bottom.

a11y.summary: A container with a soft ledge for grouping related content: a title, optional media, text and actions. Cards aren't interactive by themselves. To make a whole card open something, pass `href`: the title becomes a link whose hit area covers the card, so there is still exactly one link to tab to and one name to announce. Don't nest cards.
a11y.pattern: No ARIA widget pattern: semantic HTML. Rendered as `<article>` by default (self-contained content), labelled by its title. Use `as="section"` for a titled region of a page, or `as="div"` when the card is purely visual. The whole-card link uses the [stretched link technique](https://inclusive-components.design/cards/) rather than wrapping everything in `<a>`, which would make screen readers read the entire card as the link name.
a11y.keyboard:
| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves through interactive content inside the card (and the title link when `href` is set). The card itself is not a tab stop. |
| Enter | Follows the title link when `href` is set. |
a11y.focus: With `href`, the 3px purple focus ring is drawn around the whole card while its title link has keyboard focus (`:has(:focus-visible)`), matching the clickable area. Without `href`, only the controls inside the card take focus.
a11y.screenReader: An article is announced with its title as the name, and the title is a heading at `headingLevel` (default 3) so cards appear in the page's heading outline. With `href`, the link's name is just the title, not the whole card's text. Give `media` images real `alt` text, or `alt=""` when decorative.

examples.description: A content card with a tag, body text and an action.

components.name: CabCheckbox
components.description: A checkbox for a yes/no choice that is confirmed later (e.g. on form submit). Native `<input type="checkbox">` with a chunky custom box; native semantics are kept.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: Checked state (use `v-model`).

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label. Clicking it toggles the checkbox.

props.name: hint
props.description: Helper text linked with `aria-describedby`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the checkbox.

a11y.summary: A checkbox for an independent yes/no choice that takes effect later, usually when a form is submitted. For a setting that applies immediately, use `CabSwitch`. Group related checkboxes in a `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>`.
a11y.pattern: [WAI-ARIA APG: Checkbox](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/checkbox/), built on a native `<input type="checkbox">` so role, state and form submission come from the browser. The visible box is decorative and hidden from assistive tech.
a11y.keyboard:
| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves focus to and from the checkbox. |
| Space | Toggles checked state. |
a11y.focus: The 3px purple focus ring is drawn around the visible box (not the hidden input) on keyboard focus. The whole label is a click target, which gives a target well above 24×24px.
a11y.screenReader: Announced as "*label*, checkbox, checked/not checked". The hint is linked with `aria-describedby`. The component is controlled: the checked state shown always matches `modelValue`, so a parent that rejects a change never leaves the box out of sync.

examples.name: Basic
examples.description: A single checkbox bound with v-model.
examples.code:
<!-- A single checkbox bound with v-model. -->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CabCheckbox } from '@eltonbautista/vue'

const agreed = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <CabCheckbox v-model="agreed" label="I agree to the code of conduct" />
</template>

components.name: CabDialog
components.description: A modal dialog for a short, focused task or a confirmation that must be answered before continuing. Built on the native `<dialog>` with `showModal()`, so the page behind it is inert.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the dialog is open (use `v-model:open`).

props.name: title
props.description: Visible title; also the dialog's accessible name.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional one-line description, announced after the title.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the close button.

slots.name: default
slots.description: Dialog body. The first focusable element here receives focus on open.

slots.name: footer
slots.description: Actions row, e.g. Cancel and Confirm buttons.

a11y.summary: A modal dialog for a short task or a decision that must be made before going back to the page, like confirming a booking. Don't use it for content people may want to read alongside the page. Keep it short: a title, a sentence or a small form, and one or two actions.
a11y.pattern: [WAI-ARIA APG: Dialog (Modal)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/). Built on the native `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()`, which makes the rest of the page inert for free: it can't be clicked, focused or read while the dialog is open. Named by its title (`aria-labelledby`) and described by `description` (`aria-describedby`).
a11y.keyboard:
| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves between focusable elements inside the dialog, wrapping from last to first and first to last. |
| Escape | Closes the dialog (emits `update:open` `false`). |
| Enter / Space | Activates the focused button. |
a11y.focus: On open, focus moves to the first focusable element in the body; if there is none, it goes to the close button. Focus stays inside while the dialog is open. On close, focus returns to the element that opened it, or stays safely on the page if that element has since been removed. The close button and actions show the 3px purple focus ring.
a11y.screenReader: Announced as "*title*, dialog", followed by the description. The close button has a visually hidden text label (`closeLabel`, default "Close") and its icon is hidden from assistive tech. With reduced motion, the dialog fades instead of rising and scaling.

examples.name: Basic
examples.description: A dialog opened from a button, with a form field and actions.
examples.code:
<!-- A dialog opened from a button, with a form field and actions. -->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CabButton, CabDialog, CabTextField } from '@eltonbautista/vue'

const open = ref(false)
const name = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <CabButton @click="open = true">Save my seat</CabButton>
  <CabDialog v-model:open="open" title="Save your seat?" description="We'll hold it for 24 hours.">
    <CabTextField v-model="name" label="Name on the badge" autocomplete="name" />
    <template #footer>
      <CabButton variant="ghost" @click="open = false">Cancel</CabButton>
      <CabButton @click="open = false">Hold my seat</CabButton>
    </template>
  </CabDialog>
</template>

components.name: CabSelect
components.description: A select-only combobox: pick one value from a short list of options. Follows the APG "Select-Only Combobox" pattern; focus never leaves the combobox.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: Selected value (use `v-model`). `null` shows the placeholder.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label.

props.name: options
props.description: The options, in display order.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Text shown when nothing is selected.

props.name: hint
props.description: Helper text linked with `aria-describedby`.

props.name: error
props.description: Error message; marks the combobox invalid and is announced.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the select.

a11y.summary: Choose one value from a short list (roughly 3 to 15 options). Use it when the options don't fit comfortably as radio buttons. For long or searchable lists, a different pattern is needed. The label is always visible; the placeholder only says nothing is selected yet.
a11y.pattern: [WAI-ARIA APG: Select-Only Combobox](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/examples/combobox-select-only/). A `role="combobox"` element controls a `role="listbox"` popup. DOM focus never leaves the combobox; the highlighted option is conveyed with `aria-activedescendant`.
a11y.keyboard:
| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| ↓ / ↑ / Enter / Space / Alt+↓ | Opens the list on the selected option (or the first option). |
| Home / End | Opens the list on the first / last option. |
| ↓ / ↑ (open) | Moves to the next / previous option, skipping disabled ones. Stops at the ends. |
| Home / End (open) | Moves to the first / last option. |
| Page Down / Page Up (open) | Moves 10 options. |
| Enter / Space / Alt+↑ (open) | Selects the highlighted option and closes. |
| Tab (open) | Selects the highlighted option, closes, and moves focus on. |
| Escape (open) | Closes without changing the value. |
| Letters | Opens the list and jumps to the next option starting with the typed text (500ms buffer). |
a11y.focus: The combobox shows the 3px purple focus ring. Inside the open list, the highlighted option gets a purple inset outline and a tinted background, so it's visible without relying on colour alone. Clicking an option returns focus to the combobox. Clicking elsewhere closes the list.
a11y.screenReader: Announced as "*label*, combobox, collapsed, *selected value*". When open, each highlighted option is read as "*option*, selected/not selected, 2 of 4". Disabled options stay in the list with `aria-disabled="true"` so people know they exist. Hint and error are linked with `aria-describedby`, and errors set `aria-invalid`.

components.name: CabSwitch
components.description: An on/off switch for a setting that takes effect immediately. A `<button role="switch">` labelled by a native `<label>`.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: On/off state (use `v-model`).

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label naming the setting, e.g. "Email reminders".

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the switch.

a11y.summary: An on/off switch for a setting that takes effect immediately, like turning on reminders. If the choice is only applied when a form is submitted, use `CabCheckbox` instead: a switch promises an instant result.
a11y.pattern: [WAI-ARIA APG: Switch](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/switch/). A native `<button role="switch">` with `aria-checked`, labelled by a native `<label for>` so clicking the text also toggles it.
a11y.keyboard:
| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves focus to and from the switch. |
| Space | Toggles on/off. |
| Enter | Toggles on/off. |
a11y.focus: A 3px purple ring with a 3px offset around the track on keyboard focus. On/off is shown three ways: thumb position, track colour, and thumb colour, so it never depends on colour alone.
a11y.screenReader: Announced as "*label*, switch, on/off". With reduced motion, the thumb jumps instead of sliding; colour still changes so the state is just as clear.

examples.name: Basic
examples.code:
<!-- A switch bound with v-model. -->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CabSwitch } from '@eltonbautista/vue'

const reminders = ref(true)
</script>

<template>
  <CabSwitch v-model="reminders" label="Workshop reminders" />
</template>

components.name: CabTabs
components.description: Tabs that switch between related panels of content in place. Follows the APG Tabs pattern with roving tabindex and automatic or manual activation.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The selected tab's id (use `v-model`). Falls back to the first enabled tab if missing or disabled.

props.name: tabs
props.description: The tabs, in order.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the tab list, e.g. "Workshop details".

props.name: activation
props.description: `automatic` selects a tab as soon as it gets focus; `manual` waits for Enter or Space.

slots.name: panel
slots.description: Content for each tab's panel. Rendered once per tab; only the selected panel is visible.

a11y.summary: Tabs switch between related panels of content in the same place, like a workshop's schedule, venue and FAQ. Use them for peer content a person might compare, not for steps in a process or for site navigation.
a11y.pattern: [WAI-ARIA APG: Tabs](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/) with roving tabindex. `role="tablist"` is named by the `label` prop; each `role="tab"` controls its `role="tabpanel"`, and each panel is labelled by its tab. Activation is automatic by default (selection follows focus); set `activation="manual"` when showing a panel is slow or expensive.
a11y.keyboard:
| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves focus into the tab list (to the selected tab), then to the panel. |
| → / ← | Moves to the next / previous tab, wrapping at the ends. Disabled tabs are skipped. |
| Home / End | Moves to the first / last enabled tab. |
| Enter / Space | Selects the focused tab (manual activation). |
a11y.focus: Only the selected tab is in the tab order (`tabindex="0"`); the others are `-1` and reached with the arrow keys. Panels are focusable (`tabindex="0"`) so keyboard users can reach panels without interactive content. Both show the 3px purple focus ring. If `modelValue` is unknown or points at a disabled tab, the first enabled tab is selected so focus always has somewhere to land.
a11y.screenReader: Announced as "*label*, tab, selected, 1 of 3". Disabled tabs carry `aria-disabled="true"` and stay visible so people know the option exists. Inactive panels use the `hidden` attribute and are not read.

examples.description: Three tabs with automatic activation (selection follows focus).

examples.description: Manual activation (arrows move focus, Enter or Space selects) and a disabled tab.

components.name: CabTextField
components.description: A single-line text input with a visible label, optional hint and an error message. Errors are announced through `aria-describedby` and marked with `aria-invalid`.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: Current value (use `v-model`).

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label. Required: placeholders are not labels.

props.name: hint
props.description: Helper text shown under the label and announced after it.

props.name: error
props.description: Error message. When set, the field is marked invalid and the message is announced.

props.name: type
props.description: Native input type.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the field required (native `required` plus a visual asterisk).

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the field.

props.name: autocomplete
props.description: Native `autocomplete` token, e.g. `email` or `name`.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder example text. Never a substitute for `label` or `hint`.

a11y.summary: A single-line text input with a visible label, optional hint and error message. Use it for short free text such as names and email addresses. The label is always visible; placeholders are only for example values.
a11y.pattern: Native `<input>` with a `<label for>` association. Hint and error follow the [WAI form instructions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/instructions/) and [validation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/notifications/) guidance.
a11y.keyboard:
| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves focus to and from the field. |
| Any character | Edits the value. |
a11y.focus: A 3px purple ring with a 3px offset on keyboard focus. The border also darkens on hover. Invalid fields keep a red border and add a drawn warning icon, so colour is never the only signal.
a11y.screenReader: Announced as "*label*, edit text", plus "required" and "invalid entry" when they apply. The hint and the error are linked with `aria-describedby` (hint first, then error), so both are read after the label. The required asterisk is hidden from assistive tech because the native `required` attribute already announces it.
